a single kind of material with the same make-up all the way through, like pure water.

engage.title: ONE LETTER
engage.hook: CO is a poisonous gas. Co is a metal used in magnets. How can one small letter change everything?

reveal.question: Look at the capital letters.
reveal.answer: Co is one element, cobalt. CO is a compound: one carbon atom (C) bonded to one oxygen atom (O). A new capital letter means a new element.

learn.heading: Atoms and elements

items: The smallest part of an element that can exist. All substances are made of {k}atoms{/k}.
No chemical reaction can split an {k}element{/k} into anything simpler.
About 100 elements, all in the periodic table.

learn.imageDescription: Periodic table with groups and periods labelled

definition.text: a substance made of only one type of atom.

learn.notes: Greek 'atomos' means uncuttable (a = not, tomos = cut). Democritus suggested atoms about 2400 years ago; Dalton gave the evidence in 1803 and said each element has its own kind of atom. Periodic table: rows are periods, columns are groups.

learn.heading: Chemical symbols

items: One or two letters. The first is a capital, any second letter is lower case.
Most come from the English name: H, O, Mg, Cl.
Na natrium · K kalium · Fe ferrum · Cu cuprum
Au aurum · Ag argentum · Pb plumbum · Hg hydrargyrum

learn.imageDescription: Magnesium periodic table tile: symbol Mg, atomic number 12

examDefinition.wording: is the {1}energy{/1} needed to raise the temperature of {2}1 kg{/2} of a substance by {3}1 °C{/3}.

learn.heading: Compounds and chemical reactions

items: Always makes a NEW substance, often with an energy change (heat, light).
Only a reaction can split a compound back into its elements.
Two or more elements {k}chemically combined{/k} in fixed proportions.
Different ratio, different compound: CO and CO_2.

learn.imageDescription: Eight numbered particle diagrams, single atoms and molecules: which are elements, which are compounds?

misconception.wrong: A compound is just a mixture of its elements.
misconception.right: In a compound the atoms are joined, in a fixed ratio. A mixture's parts are not joined.

definition.text: a long chain molecule made of many repeating units.

learn.heading: Iron + sulfur

videoLink.text: Iron and sulfur react to form iron sulfide

toWatch: The colour of iron and of sulfur, and which one a magnet picks up.
What happens once the reaction starts, even after the flame is removed.
The colour of the product, and whether a magnet picks it up.
learn.prompt: Mixture or compound? What is your evidence?

questions.q: Write the word equation for the reaction.
Give two signs that a chemical reaction happened.
questions.a: It glowed (gave out heat and light); a new black solid formed that is not magnetic.

questions.q: Why can a magnet separate the iron and sulfur mixture but not iron sulfide?
questions.a: In the mixture the iron is not bonded, so it keeps its magnetism. In iron sulfide the atoms are bonded into a new compound.

options: A. A substance made of only one type of atom
B. Two or more elements chemically combined
C. Two substances mixed but not chemically joined
D. The smallest part of a substance that can exist
build.explanation: An element contains only one type of atom.
build.commonError: Choosing D, which is close to the definition of an atom.

why.D: that is the definition of an atom

build.q: Which of these is a compound?
build.explanation: H_2O contains two elements, hydrogen and oxygen, bonded together.
build.commonError: Choosing O_2 because it has two atoms; both atoms are oxygen, so it is an element.

why.A: thinks two atoms joined means a compound
why.B: thinks a metal must be a compound

build.q: How many atoms are in one molecule of ethanol, C_2H_6O?
build.commonError: Answering 8 by missing the O, which has no number so counts as 1.

why.A: counts the elements, not the atoms
why.B: adds the numbers and forgets the O
why.D: adds an extra 3 for the three elements

build.q: What is the difference between Co and CO?
options: A. Co and CO are both the element cobalt.
B. Co is the element cobalt; CO is a compound.
C. Co is a compound; CO is the element cobalt.
D. Co and CO are both compounds of carbon.
build.explanation: A new capital letter means a new element, so CO contains C and O.

why.D: reads C as carbon in both

build.q: Iron filings and sulfur powder are mixed but not heated. How could you separate them?
options: B. Pull the iron out with a magnet
C. It cannot be done without a reaction
D. Melt the iron and pour it off
build.explanation: In a mixture the iron is not bonded, so it keeps its magnetism.
build.commonError: Choosing A: heating makes iron sulfide, a compound.

why.A: heating makes a compound, so they can no longer be separated
why.C: thinks a mixture is already joined

build.q: What is the chemical symbol for lead?
build.explanation: Pb comes from its Latin name, plumbum.
build.commonError: Using the first letters of the English name.

why.C: takes the first two letters of lead

build.instruction: Element or compound? Then look at the endings: what do -ide and -ate tell you?

worked.prompt: Magnesium burns in oxygen. Name the product and write the word equation.
steps: Metal first, keeps its name: magnesium
Non-metal second, ending changes to -ide: oxygen 	o oxide
-ate means oxygen is in it too: potassium sulfate = K, S and O

yourTurn.prompt: Sodium reacts with chlorine. Name the product and write the word equation.

worked.prompt: How many atoms of each element are in H_{2}SO_{4}?
steps: Split at each capital letter: H_2 · S · O_4
O_4 = 4 oxygen atoms. Total = 7 atoms of 3 elements

yourTurn.prompt: How many atoms of each element are in CaCO_3?
yourTurn.answer: 1 calcium, 1 carbon, 3 oxygen = 5 atoms of 3 elements

build.instruction: Which show a chemical reaction? Sort them, then name the sign that a new substance formed.

developing.q: Define the terms atom, element and compound.
developing.a: Atom: smallest part of an element that can exist. Element: only one type of atom. Compound: two or more elements chemically combined.

developing.q: Give the symbols for iron, sodium and lead. Why do they not match the English names?
developing.a: Fe, Na, Pb. They come from Latin names: ferrum, natrium, plumbum.

developing.q: Sort into elements and compounds: Fe, H_2O, O_2, NaCl, N_2, CH_4.
developing.a: Elements: Fe, O_2, N_2. Compounds: H_2O, NaCl, CH_4.

reaching.q: How many atoms of each element are in glucose, C_6H_12O_6? How many atoms in total?
Draw particle diagrams of Co and CO. Explain the difference.
reaching.a: Co: single atoms all the same, an element. CO: molecules of one C bonded to one O, a compound.

reaching.q: Name the compound formed when calcium reacts with oxygen. Write the word equation.
reaching.a: Calcium oxide. calcium + oxygen \to calcium oxide

mastering.q: A magnet separates iron from an iron and sulfur mixture, but not from iron sulfide. Explain why.
mastering.a: In the mixture iron is not bonded, so keeps its properties. In iron sulfide it is bonded into a new compound with new properties.

mastering.q: Fool's gold is FeS_2. The black solid made from iron and sulfur is FeS. Explain why these are different compounds.
mastering.a: Compounds have fixed proportions. FeS has 1 Fe to 1 S; FeS_2 has 1 Fe to 2 S. A different ratio is a different compound.

mastering.q: A bracket multiplies everything inside it. How many atoms are in Mg(OH)_2? Show your working.
